# Apple Signing, Entitlements & Notarization

Also use when the user mentions 'app not opening', 'damaged app', 'unidentified developer', 'notarization ticket', 'hardened runtime exception', 'library validation', 'team id mismatch', 'provisioning profile expired', or 'notarytool submit'.

## Why this skill exists

Measured 2026-08-26, zeststream-cast: a fully **notarized, stapled, Gatekeeper-accepted** macOS bundle
in which **every one of six binaries exited 137 (`Killed: 9`)** on launch. It cost most of a working
day and produced **four wrong diagnoses in sequence** — by three different agents plus the
orchestrator — before the mechanism was found.

The buyer-visible cost: no fresh bundle could be installed at all, which blocked four beads whose
acceptance required a current installed artifact.

Joshua: *"lets make sure this is locked into our apple skills so we dont have to repeat this next
time we have a similar project."*

---

## THE ONE-PARAGRAPH ANSWER

**A provisioning profile authorizes a restricted entitlement for the bundle's MAIN EXECUTABLE ONLY.**
If your build signs every binary in `Contents/MacOS/` from one `--entitlements` file, the helper
binaries carry a restricted key that no profile covers, and **AMFI SIGKILLs them with no message, no
crash report, and no amfid log entry**. Scope the restricted entitlement to the main executable and
give helpers their own minimal plist.

Both halves are required: the **profile** (necessary) AND **per-binary scoping** (also necessary).
Neither alone is sufficient.

---

## THE DIAGNOSTIC LADDER — run in this order, do not skip

Each rung isolates ONE variable. Skipping rungs is how four wrong diagnoses happened.

```bash
B=YourApp.app/Contents/MacOS/YourBinary

# 0. Is it actually SIGKILL, and from outside?
bash -c "$B --version; echo rc=\$?"      # "Killed: 9" + rc=137 = external kill
lldb -b -o "run --version" -- "$B"       # "exited with status = 9" = kernel, lldb cannot catch it

# 1. Do OTHER binaries in the same bundle run? THE HIGHEST-VALUE RUNG.
for b in YourApp.app/Contents/MacOS/*; do "$b" --version >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "$(basename $b) rc=$?"; done
#   Some run, some die  -> PER-BINARY entitlement scoping. You are done; go to THE FIX.
#   ALL die             -> bundle-level: missing/mismatched profile, or unsigned on arm64.

# 2. What is ACTUALLY on the failing binary right now?
codesign -dv "$B" 2>&1 | grep -E "flags|Authority|Identifier"
codesign -d --entitlements - "$B" 2>/dev/null

# 3. Is a profile present AND sealed by the signature?
ls -la YourApp.app/Contents/embedded.provisionprofile
codesign -d --entitlements - YourApp.app 2>/dev/null | grep -c application-identifier

# 4. Does the profile grant the entitlement, for THIS app id?
security cms -D -i YourApp.app/Contents/embedded.provisionprofile > /tmp/pp.plist
/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Print :Entitlements:com.apple.application-identifier" /tmp/pp.plist
grep -c "com.apple.developer.system-extension.install" /tmp/pp.plist
```

---

## THE FIVE TRAPS THAT PRODUCED THE WRONG ANSWERS

Every one of these cost real hours. They are listed because each is individually plausible.

### 1. `spctl`, `stapler` and notarization are ALL BLIND to this
The failing bundle was genuinely `accepted / source=Notarized Developer ID`, `stapler validate`
worked, `codesign --verify --deep --strict` was clean — while every binary died. **Gatekeeper
validates provenance, not launchability.** The only check that catches it is EXECUTING each binary
after signing. Add that gate; nothing else substitutes.

### 2. Copying a binary out of the bundle to test it CHANGES TWO VARIABLES
`cp` out + run "works" -> tempting conclusion: "the bundle is the problem." False. Copying forces
an ad-hoc re-sign that silently drops **both** the entitlement and the hardened-runtime flag. Always
`codesign -d --entitlements -` on the exact artifact you launched, and say what it showed.

### 3. On Apple Silicon, an UNSIGNED arm64 binary is ALWAYS killed
So "unsigned also dies" proves **nothing** and is not a valid control. The valid control is
**ad-hoc signed** (`codesign -f -s -`), never unsigned.

### 4. Signing the BINARY does not seal a profile into the BUNDLE
`codesign` on `Contents/MacOS/x` leaves `Contents/embedded.provisionprofile` outside the seal. Sign
the **bundle** (`codesign ... YourApp.app`). Verify the profile is sealed post-sign, not merely
present — the ordering bug leaves an "embed" step looking green.

### 5. `AMFIUnserializeXML` is stricter than `plutil`
A double hyphen `--` inside an XML comment is illegal XML. `plutil -lint` says OK; codesign says
`AMFIUnserializeXML: syntax error` and **exits 1**. With `2>/dev/null` the binary silently keeps its
PREVIOUS signature — you believe you re-signed clean and it still dies.
**Never suppress stderr on codesign. Always check its exit code.**

---

## THE FIX

```
Sources/App/Resources/entitlements.plist         # main executable: restricted keys + camera/mic
Sources/App/Resources/entitlements-helper.plist  # helpers: NO restricted keys
Sources/App/Resources/entitlements-dev.plist     # --dev-sign: NO restricted keys (needs no profile)
```

In the signing loop: main executable gets `entitlements.plist`; every other binary in
`Contents/MacOS/` gets `entitlements-helper.plist`. Embed the profile BEFORE signing, then sign the
bundle so the profile is sealed.

**Do NOT "fix" this by deleting the restricted entitlement from the main executable** — that
silently regresses the feature it exists for (e.g. the system extension can no longer activate).

---

## GATES THAT MUST SHIP WITH IT (all mutation-proven)

| Gate | Refuses when | Why nothing else catches it |
|---|---|---|
| `bundle-binary-sigkilled` | any binary exits 137 post-sign | **the only check that catches this class** |
| `entitlements-amfi-unparseable` | codesign cannot parse the plist | `plutil -lint` passes illegal XML |
| `provisioning-profile-app-id-mismatch` | profile app-id ≠ bundle id | wrong-id profile embeds, notarizes, staples clean, then SIGKILLs identically to no profile |
| `provisioning-profile-unsealed` | profile present but outside the signature | embed-after-sign looks green |
| `helper-entitlements-missing` | release build without the helper plist | silent regression to one-plist-for-all |

**The error text is part of the fix.** The original failure reported `"ffmpeg not resolving"` while
every binary was exiting 137 — that lie is what misdirected the investigation for hours. Name the
real cause in the marker.

---

## PORTAL SETUP (each nested bundle needs its OWN App ID + profile)

1. **Identifiers** → ⊕ → App IDs → App → **Explicit** → exact bundle id → tick the capability
   (e.g. **System Extension**; NOT any `DriverKit *` row, those are development-only).
   The Description field is NOT the Bundle ID — they sit adjacent and get transposed.
2. Repeat for **each nested bundle**: a `.systemextension` under
   `Contents/Library/SystemExtensions/` has its own `CFBundleIdentifier` and needs its own App ID.
   **Read the identifier off the shipped bundle, never from memory** — ours was
   `...installer.virtual-camera`, not `...installer.virtual`.
3. **Profiles** → ⊕ → Distribution → **Developer ID** → that App ID → Developer ID Application cert.
4. **Verify before building** (a profile lacking the entitlement leaves you exactly where you started):
   ```bash
   security cms -D -i x.provisionprofile | grep -c "com.apple.developer.system-extension.install"
   ```
5. **TRACK the profiles in git.** They contain **no private key** (verify: `grep "PRIVATE KEY"` → 0);
   they are signed public authorizations. Untracked = "correct on exactly one disk", and a
   `--source-revision` build from `git archive` will not find them.

---

## NOTARIZATION CREDENTIALS

Uses an **App Store Connect API key** (Key ID + **Issuer ID** + .p8), not a Developer key — see
[[apple-asc-api-credentials]] for the resolver and the 401 trauma class.

```bash
xcrun notarytool store-credentials <profile> --key <p8> --key-id <id> --issuer <uuid>
xcrun notarytool history --key <p8> --key-id <id> --issuer <uuid>   # proves auth before a 15-min build
```
The Issuer ID is per-team and is NOT derivable from the .p8. If it is missing, check the login
keychain — a prior project on the same team may have stored the tuple:
`security dump-keychain | grep -i "issuer_id"`.

---

## WHAT "DONE" MEANS

Not `spctl accepted`. Not `Notarization status: Accepted`. Not `stapler validate worked`.
All four were true while every binary died.

**Done is:** every binary in `Contents/MacOS/` launches with RC≠137, proven by a gate that executes
them, on the notarized artifact you actually ship.

## Framework Selection

| Scenario | Signing identity | Profile | When to use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shipping to users | Developer ID Application | Developer ID distribution | production releases; notarization required |
| Internal testing | Apple Development | Development | dev machines only; no notarization |
| Quick local run | Ad-hoc (`-s -`) | None | smoke test; never ships |
| Restricted entitlement | Developer ID Application | Developer ID + capability | system extensions, DriverKit |
| Fastest iteration | Ad-hoc (`-s -`) | None | proves launchability without profile |

## Entitlement Scoping

| Binary | Entitlements file | Restricted keys | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main executable | entitlements.plist | Yes (profile-covered) | profile authorizes the main executable only |
| Helper binaries | entitlements-helper.plist | No | restricted key without profile cover means AMFI SIGKILL |
| Dev builds | entitlements-dev.plist | No | no profile needed; fastest iteration |

## Diagnostic Outcomes

| Ladder result | Conclusion | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Some binaries run, some die (137) | Per-binary entitlement scoping fault | go to THE FIX |
| All binaries die (137) | Bundle-level: profile or signature | check profile presence and seal |
| `codesign --verify` fails | Signature broken | re-sign; never suppress stderr |
| Profile app-id differs from bundle id | Wrong profile embedded | re-issue for the exact bundle id |
| `AMFIUnserializeXML` error | Entitlements plist malformed | fix XML, re-sign, check exit code |

## Provisioning Profiles

| Profile type | Distribution | Restricted entitlements | Use for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Developer ID | Outside App Store | Yes, with capability | shipping signed apps |
| Development | Registered devices | Basic only | local debugging |
| Ad-hoc | None | No | testing only; never ships |

## Anti-Patterns

| Anti-Pattern | Why It Fails | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Trusting spctl/stapler as launch proof | Gatekeeper validates provenance, not launchability | execute every binary post-sign |
| Testing by copying a binary out of the bundle | `cp` forces ad-hoc re-sign, silently dropping entitlements | inspect the exact shipped artifact |
| Using an unsigned binary as the arm64 control | unsigned arm64 always SIGKILLs; proves nothing | the valid control is ad-hoc signed (`-s -`) |
| Signing the binary instead of the bundle | profile sits outside the signature seal | sign the `.app` bundle |
| Suppressing codesign stderr | hides `AMFIUnserializeXML` parse failures | never `2>/dev/null`; check the exit code |
| Deleting the restricted entitlement to "fix" | silently regresses the feature it enables | scope it to the

# beads-north-star — the Jeff-bead standard (durable home)

> **This is the canonical home.** The `beads-br` skill (jsm-managed) carries a mirror
> of this NORTH STAR section that may lag or vanish on the next `jsm install-all
> --force` — it already got wiped once (2026-06-23) and was restored in place as a
> stopgap on 2026-07-01. Do not edit `beads-br`'s SKILL.md to fix drift; fix it here
> and repoint CLAUDE.md's router at this file instead.

Reverse-engineered firsthand from Jeff Emanuel's 11.2k-bead `bv` cockpit (2026-06-17).
**A bead is a SELF-CONTAINED SPEC, not a title.** The full standard + adoption plan:
`~/Developer/foundry/mission/beadflow/JEFF-BEAD-STANDARD-2026-06-17.md`.

## ⛔ `--actor <YourAgentName>` ON EVERY `br` WRITE — NEVER LET IT DEFAULT

**Joshua, 2026-09-07:** *"i dont complete tasks, we shouldn't allow agents to put josh"*

`br` falls back to the **ambient git identity** for `created_by`. A fleet shares one
checkout and therefore one git identity, so every write lands under the human's name.
Measured that day in `uds`:

```
created_by:  156 josh | 48 SapphireIsland | 9 SageCastle | 2 CrimsonCarp | 2 CloudyGrove
assignee:    211 null | 2 SapphireIsland | 2 CloudyGrove | 1 pane3-luna | 1 josh
```

**72% of 217 beads credited the one person who did none of the work.** There is **no
`BEADS_ACTOR` env var** (checked the binary), so the flag is the only lever, and nothing
notices when you omit it.

```bash
br create "..." --actor PinkGorge        # -> created_by=PinkGorge   (proven: uds-508b)
br create "..."                          # -> created_by=josh        (the human, silently)
```

Pass it on **every** write — `create`, `update`, `close`, `comments add`.

**IT IS NOT COSMETIC — IT DEFEATS NON-AUTHOR GRADING.** Grading routes on authorship.
`uds-head-vs-tree-e4qy` read `created_by=josh` while another agent had implemented it;
routing a grader off that field hands an agent **their own bead** and the audit trail
looks *clean* while the closer grades their own work. **So `created_by` is not evidence
of authorship** — when picking a bead to grade, read the bead's comments or ask, never
that field alone.

**Do NOT retro-attribute legacy rows by guess.** Fabricated provenance is worse than
absent provenance (same class as an rch commit stamp that resolves in no repo). Scope any
enforcing detector to a cutoff commit so legacy rows cannot make it vacuously red and get
it disabled.

## CREATE — every non-trivial bead body carries WHAT / WHY / ACCEPTANCE, plus labels

```bash
# -l is MANDATORY (bv navigation) — every `\` below is followed only by a newline (copy-paste-safe;
# a `\` with a trailing inline comment silently breaks the line-continuation).
br create "B6: wire-format conformance harness" \
  --slug wire-format-conformance -t feature -p 1 \
  -l conformance,testing \
  --parent flywheel-<epic> --deps blocks:flywheel-<x> \
  -d 'WHAT: (a) specify wire format; (b) golden/round-trip conformance harness.
WHY: prevents silent drift; public fns currently untested.
ACCEPTANCE: harness green (round-trip+golden+boundary+negative); no public fn/transition lacks a test (AUDITED).'
```

- **WHAT** = the deliverable (enumerate (a)/(b) if multi-part). **WHY** = the pain / what it unblocks.
- **ACCEPTANCE = coverage-shaped, MEASURED, not vibes** — "harness green", "no fn lacks a test", a specific
  closeable condition. This is the close-verify floor (DNA-match to rigor.py / the non-vacuity law).
- **ACCEPTANCE's fires-on-known-bad must be an IN-TREE specimen, never an external apply-patch harness**
  (Jeff's mature-Rust pattern, corpus-grounded 2026-07-06 from frankensqlite / franken_markdown / beads_rust).
  A gate proves it BITES via a `#[test]` that asserts the guard refuses a planted bad input, a trybuild
  compile-fail, or a `--self-test` mode that writes a TEMP fixture and asserts rejection — **never a
  `.patch` + `git apply` + worktree harness.** `git apply` silently no-ops when the patch index-hash misses
  HEAD, so the specimen doesn't fire: a fires-on-known-bad that can't fire is a *fooled certificate = Sev-0*,
  and patches rot against every refactor. Prove-it-bites test: *deleting the guard must turn a test RED*
  (curated `cargo-mutants` on the guard module — not the whole crate — is the tool where a silent hole is Sev-0).
  Prefer **ratchets over thresholds** (a committed monotonic floor / survivor-ceiling that can only improve,
  plus a drift guard tying the number the binary advertises to the number the gate enforces); keep the
  orchestrator (gate.sh / xtask) THIN — assertions live in the tests, not the shell. Full standard + citations:
  the target repo's `docs/RIGOR-STACK.md` (fp's is the reference exemplar).
- **Always `-l <labels>`** (topical, lowercase). **`--slug`** for a readable hierarchical ID. `--parent`/`--deps` for the graph.

## DAG — build backward from the product, then attack closure

A DAG is an execution argument, not a task list. It can be complete only relative to the questions it
planned; never claim absolute completeness.

**Build it:**

1. Start from the buyer-visible terminal outcome and decompose backward. Every leaf must produce an
   input a successor needs, remove a named blocker, or be the terminal product. Presence alone is not
   progress: record the pre-state and require a transition, new call site, or retired incumbent.
2. Add `blocks:` only when the successor cannot satisfy its acceptance without the predecessor's
   output. Put independent checks in cost order: build/import/install before semantic qualification;
   the cheapest falsifier should kill the branch first.
3. Keep the graph reviewable with `bv --robot-plan`, `bv --robot-insights`, and `br graph --all`.
   Before closing the parent, account for every leaf and every blocked terminal; a satisfied
   prerequisite cannot stand in for the closing bead's product.

**Attack each close:**

1. Make acceptance non-vacuous. Demonstrate that the named work changes the pre-state; a condition
   already true before the bead began cannot close it.
2. Make negatives causal. Neutralize unrelated failure preconditions, assert the named detector and
   branch-specific marker, then bypass that detector and prove the same broad RED no longer passes the
   fixture. A nonzero exit alone is not evidence.
3. Bind evidence to the exact source snapshot, executable/artifact identity, and mutable dependency
   identity it tested. Isolate concurrent build outputs. If a bound input moves, revalidate or reopen;
   do not inherit the old green or substitute a fixed age threshold.
4. Assert buyer-visible semantics at the final boundary. For rendered numbers, test the rendered
   label/denominator and audit correct as well as defective sites. For retrieval, token presence is not
   semantic agreement; include a negation control such as `without X`.
5. Reserve one outside-the-plan challenge before epic closure: ask what the real product reads, writes,
   or exposes against its primary buyer data. A planned fixture can catch a defect in what was built;
   it cannot prove the team built the right thing. A new answer becomes a bead, not a retroactive claim
   that the original DAG was complete.
6. Wire each gate to the graph edge controlling the next decision its evidence can invalidate. Ask:
   *what does this stop someone doing tomorrow?* The runtime-backed report/gate in
   `polymarket-pico-z@125d23f2fa96e46d0076e9785979fcf8d7123eba:PLAN-EDGE-MEASUREMENT.md:49-86` had
   zero resolved trades and said no more code before 500, yet the gate at
   `polymarket-pico-z@0944915eebca91cced6496e32d8b1ea1de22cc6d:src/engine/sports_go_live_gate.py:75-147`
   blocked real-money launch, not construction, and was archived on 2026-04-08. Evidence still did
   not establish edge on 2026-04-11, while R16/R18 were CLEAN with zero criticals or mediums
   (`polymarket-pico-z@125d23f2fa96e46d0076e9785979fcf8d7123eba:PLAN-REVIEWS/round18-adversarial.md:96-114`).
   Contrast `bughunt-platform-plan@1933524b05123ffc1d7985a106a22d2ada5a73f3:.flywheel/CHARTER.md:7-47`,
   whose premise review halted construction. A terminal-only gate is a gate on nothing while distant.

**Measured sources** (all in `~/Developer/franken-harvest`): bead `fh-xjj` (presence passed while
adoption stayed zero), `standards/causal-known-bads.md` and bead `fh-kkf` (11/24 to 24/24 causal),
`standards/hermetic-shared-tree-tests.md` and bead `fh-t36` (stale binary passed 2/2), bead `fh-ost`
(53 upstream moves/30d; median 12.49h), bead `fh-vyl` (cheap filter removed 3/5 before qualification),
and bead `fh-1v5` (luv-diet rendered, negation, and unplanned-question evidence).

**Rejected, deliberately:** a universal 12.49-hour expiry (C20 supplied a measured cadence, not a
portable clock); C33/C34's literal food/UI wording as separate DAG rules (their boundary patterns are
retained above); and a mandatory DAG-proof document or meta-bead (it would manufacture an artifact
solely for checking). No other measured candidate was discarded.

## REVIEW / READ / PLAN — `bv` is the planning BRAIN, not just a list

Jeff's cockpit; we underuse it:

```bash
# the navigation half — how Jeff reads/plans an 11k beadbase (all --robot-* = JSON for agents):
bv --robot-triage                 # unified ranked work + evidence (THE default; what to do)
bv --robot-next                   # the single best next bead
bv --robot-plan                   # dependency-respecting execution ORDER
bv --robot-priority               # priority recommendations
bv --robot-insights               # graph analysis: centrality, impact, structure (the per-bead metrics)
bv --robot-triage-by-track        # group by execution track (multi-agent coordination)
bv -r actionable | high-impact    # named recipes
bv -l <label> --robot-insights    # SCOPE analysis to one label's subgraph (needs labels — see Step 3)
bv --severity warning --alert-type stale_issue   # the ALERTS surface (Jeff's "⚠ N alerts")
br scheduler --json               # explainable ranked dispatch for swarms (PageRank + staleness + fairness)
br show <id> --json   ·   br ready --json   ·   br blocked --json   ·   br graph --all
```

A HUMAN watches the fleet with bare `bv` (the full-screen TUI cockpit — his screen). An AGENT never runs
bare `bv` (blocks in TUI) — always `bv --robot-*`. **`-l <label>` scoping + the alert surface only work if
beads are labeled** — our labels are at 32% with 1,199-label sprawl; consolidation is the Step-3 enabler.

## HANDLE — the audit trail lives IN the bead

Our biggest gap: only 8% have comments; Jeff's are the norm.

```bash
br comments add flywheel-<id> "COVERAGE AUDIT (read-only): 82/84 paths covered; round-trip+golden green. \
VERDICT: satisfied; 2 gaps low-risk. @<agent> hold 2 tests."   # at every close/checkpoint
br close flywheel-<id> --reason "<what+proof>"                   # reason carries WHAT + the proof/receipt
```

At every close or checkpoint, add a comment with a **VERDICT** — don't bury the verification in commits/chat.

**The verb is `br comments` (PLURAL). `br comment` never posts — and its failure exits 0.**
`comment` is clap **prefix-matching** to `comments`, so your text lands where a *subcommand* was
expected. Both forms below pass a body correctly; `--file` is for long or quote-heavy text, not a
requirement:

```bash
br comments add <id> "VERDICT: …"          # correct — positional string persists
br comments add <id> --file <path>         # correct — same thing, for long/quote-heavy bodies
br comment     <id> "VERDICT: …"           # NEVER

# zeststream-pr — upstream contributions: pick the artifact, prove it, submit it, follow through

<!-- TOC: FOREVER-RULE | Hard Rules | EXACT PROMPTS | Decision Tree | Lifecycle | Authorship | PR Body | Contracts | Expectations | Track Record | Anti-Patterns | Scripts | References -->

> **Core insight.** A maintainer's review time is the scarce resource, and every artifact we send
> spends some of it. The repo's own contract decides which artifact is welcome. Proof decides whether it
> survives review. The human owner's words decide whether it is trusted. Our record is the evidence:
> **0 of 15** upstream PRs merged. On Dicklesworthstone repos Jeffrey closed all 10 he acted on,
> citing his no-outside-PRs policy. Yet **102 of 116** closed issues ended in a referenced fix. The
> difference was not code quality. It was sending the artifact the contract asks for
> (`references/CASE-STUDIES.md`). Every rule below is tagged **[measured here]**, **[external]** (cited
> in `references/RESEARCH.md`) or **[awaiting upstream]**.

## FOREVER-RULE: NO upstream write without this skill

Joshua, 2026-04-27: "we cannot submit PRs without this." Extended 2026-09-25 to every public write
to a repo we don't own: PRs, issues, comments, review replies. The jeff-issue chain
(Dicklesworthstone repos) is now part of this skill: `references/ISSUE-FILING.md` and
`references/MAINTAINER-RESPONSE.md` keep its phase names.

## Hard Rules

1. **Read the contract before writing code.** CONTRIBUTING, AGENTS/CLAUDE.md, PR and issue templates,
   AI policy, the README "contributions" section, SECURITY. The repo's rules override this skill.
   Record the URL and the date you read it; re-read on submission day because policies change monthly
   [external: Ghostty tightened twice in 5 months; about half of 92 tracked AI-policy files were revised].
2. **Dedup before diagnosis, and before anything else.** Run `gh issue list --state all`,
   `gh pr list --state all`, the release list, open PRs touching the same files, and
   `git log origin/main -- <path>` the moment you have a symptom, before reading docs or building a
   repro. Check which binary you actually ran (`type -a <tool>`, each one's version) [measured: the am
   hang vs #203, fixed and released 4 h earlier; a stale `br` 0.2.17 shadowing 0.6.0 replayed our own
   closed beads_rust#497].
3. **No finding leaves without a stranger-reproducible repro.** Verify your own instrument first
   (selector exists, exit code checked, count not paged). No repro means a bead, not a filing
   [measured: two public retractions, cass#363 after 3 min and frankensqlite#298 after 53 min].
4. **One logical change per PR.** Refactors go in a separate PR, tests go in the same one. Dependent
   work is a stacked PR that says "builds on #N". Above ~400 changed production lines, split it or get
   consent first [external: Google says ~100 lines is fine and ~1000 too large; measured: our 3.4k-line
   ntm PRs were withdrawn within 7 minutes].
5. **Old paths stay old, and a test proves it.** Every change carries a parity test showing that
   callers outside the fix behave exactly as before: call counts, ordering, what hooks see. Identical
   visible output is not proof [measured: PR 2 review findings F1 and F6].
6. **Run the real product, not only the suite.** A test that fails before and passes after, then an
   A/B run of the real CLI with near-miss controls (`references/PROOF-LADDER.md`) [external: omp
   CONTRIBUTING says "`bun check` passes by itself is not sufficient"].
7. **A second agent reviews adversarially before Josh sees it,** and every finding closes with a test
   that failed before and passes after [measured: F1, F5 and F6 were all found this way].
8. **The human owns the words where the contract says so.** Josh writes whatever the contract says a
   human writes (Tier A repos, and the own-words sentence on Tier B PRs such as omp). Agents never
   write a substitute for those words and never add a sign-off [external: Rust bans LLM-originated
   descriptions; the kernel says AI must never add Signed-off-by; LLVM bans agents that act without
   human approval]. Where the contract sets no human-authorship rule (Dicklesworthstone issues and
   replies), agents write and post under this skill's gates.
9. **Disclose AI assistance in the form the repo asks for** (`Assisted-by:`, a label, or a sentence).
   Turn off tool-default trailers where the repo forbids them [external: Mesa forbids `Co-authored-by`
   for AI; Claude Code adds one by default].
10. **This skill's gates are the approval** (Joshua, 2026-10-01: "i dont need to approve - i built the
    skill - we follow that"). Issues, comments and replies go out once the gates pass: dedup, the
    Report Test, the rubric `pass`, the dry run, then readback. For issues the agent runs
    `jeff-issue.py approve` itself after those gates; the single-use token still binds approval to the
    exact bytes. No per-packet sign-off from Josh. The exception is a repo whose CONTRIBUTING requires
    a human to review or submit (omp: "submit the pull request only after that review, rather than
    letting an agent publish it autonomously"); there the contract wins and the PR goes up on Josh's
    per-PR go-ahead, and the agent always reads back what landed.
11. **Read back what landed:** the first lines of the live body and the diff on the fork
    [measured: skillranker#4 went live with `DRAFT — NOT SUBMITTED` on a rubric pass 7/7].
12. **After opening: changelog when the repo wants it, a ledger row, the watcher. Ping at most once,
    after 7 days or more, and never to ask for an ETA** [external: kernel, LLVM and opensource.guide
    set one-week minimums].
13. **Keep volume low.** One or two open items per repo; the first PR to a project builds trust
    [external: matplotlib calls parallel breadth across projects unacceptable; GitHub now caps open
    PRs per user].

## THE EXACT PROMPT — Build and submit a PR

```
Use the zeststream-pr skill to take <change> to an upstream PR on <owner/repo>.
1. Phase 0: dedup with --state all (issues, PRs, releases, main log, open PRs on the same files).
   Cite the commands and hit counts; a count equal to --limit is capped, not a total.
2. Phase 1: read the contract (references/CONTRIBUTION-CONTRACT.md). Classify the repo STOP /
   ISSUE-ONLY / GATED / CONDITIONAL and set the authorship tier. Not PR-accepting: switch to the issue path.
3. Clean clone at upstream HEAD, reproduce, and write a test in upstream's own suite that fails.
4. Minimal fix, one logical change, plus a parity test for callers outside the fix.
5. Climb references/PROOF-LADDER.md for the change type. Keep receipts under the lab dir.
6. Hand the branch to a second agent for adversarial review. Close every finding with a test that
   fails before and passes after.
7. git fetch; draft the body from references/PR-BODY-TEMPLATE.md with the owner-words slot EMPTY;
   run `bash scripts/pr-preflight.sh` until 0 FAIL and every READ item is read. Don't commit if the
   repo's AGENTS.md says "never commit unless asked" until Josh asks (omp AGENTS.md:260).
8. Stop. Show Josh the diff, the proof, and the preflight output. Ask for his words and his go-ahead.
Never push, fork, comment, or open anything before step 8 is approved.
```

## Decision Tree — which artifact, if any

```
Symptom or improvement for a repo we don't own
├─ Dedup hit, closed and released ........ upgrade; no filing (record the version bump)
├─ Dedup hit, open ....................... comment only with materially new evidence, else nothing
├─ Contract: AI contributions banned (Zig, Gentoo, NetBSD, QEMU, GNOME extensions; git rejects AI-looking work)
│                                        → stop. Nothing upstream; keep a local patch or talk to Josh
├─ Contract: no outside PRs (Dicklesworthstone/*; tldraw closes external PRs)
│                                        → ISSUE path: repro, root cause, file:line. A patch only illustrates
├─ Contract: PRs gated (Ghostty needs a vouch + accepted issue; Rust needs a pre-arranged reviewer)
│                                        → do the gate first, in Josh's words, then the PR path
├─ Contract: PRs welcome, issue-first forbidden (can1357/oh-my-pi: robomp turns issues into its own PRs)
│                                        → PR path directly; file an issue only if we won't fix it
├─ Change adds public surface (extension-visible hook, config key, CLI flag), changes a default,
│  or spans packages ....................... discussion first (Discord, RFC, issue), per the contract;
│                                           internal wiring for a bug fix is not public surface — say so in the body
└─ Otherwise ............................. PR path
```

3:## Purpose
4:
5:UDS has one ordered verdict chain. It answers whether the repository is measurable and what stopped
6:measurement; it does not convert a refusal, timeout, or missing input into a product PASS.
7:## Gate wiring
8:
9:The tracked scripts/check.sh dispatcher is the canonical ordered consumer of this contract. The repository pre-commit wrapper is githooks/pre-commit; the commit-message wrapper is githooks/commit-msg; both delegate to tracked executable implementations. Each gate must preserve the typed exit lattice and carry a fires-on-known-bad leg.
10:
11:The pre-commit implementation checks staged whitespace with `git diff --cached --check`, then invokes the existing autofix tool with `--check --staged --repo`. Check mode does not rewrite worktree files or restage partial edits. The external helper selects staged path names but currently reads their worktree bytes; general staged-blob formatter isolation is not established. Staged-deletion and Beads JSONL guards remain required.

13:## Gate sentence
14:
15:The chain is the existing `scripts/check.sh` stage sequence. `closure` is last because it joins the
16:registry, planning spine, bead graph, and scorecard. A failed earlier stage blocks later stages;
17:blocked is not a verdict for the blocked subject.
18:
19:```text
20:fmt -> clippy -> test -> registry-check -> neg-evidence-gate -> close-evidence-gate
21:    -> dag-validate-gate -> build-intent -> claims-lint -> conformance -> build-placement
22:    -> artifact-platform -> close-cites -> bead-commit-check -> scorecard-promotion
23:    -> review-lineage-check -> closure

26:Seventeen stages, copied from the `STAGES=(...)` array at `scripts/check.sh:16` rather than
27:restated from memory. The `G1`-`G11` contracts below name **eleven** of them. The other six are
28:`neg-evidence-gate`, `close-evidence-gate` and `dag-validate-gate` (documented under *House gate
29:wiring*), plus `artifact-platform`, `bead-commit-check` and `review-lineage-check`, which have **no
30:gate contract in this document**. That gap is stated rather than hidden: a chain longer than its
31:contract is how a stage runs with nobody able to say what it reads.

33:## Typed result law
34:
35:The typed exit lattice is defined by `crates/uds/src/lib.rs`:
36:
37:| code | meaning | law |
38:|---|---|---|
39:| `EC-PASS` | the operation ran and succeeded | only a completed positive verdict |
40:| `EC-RED` | a named guard or genuine gated defect fired | subject failure, not a count |
41:| `EC-USAGE` | the invocation was invalid | repair the caller |
42:| `EC-LOCKED` | another writer/build holds the lease | `EL-LOCK-IS-NOT-FAILURE` |
43:| `EC-UNRUN` | the subject could not be measured | `EL-UNRUN-IS-NOT-RED` |
44:| `EC-INFRA` | the gate's own machinery failed | `EL-INFRA-IS-NOT-SUBJECT` |
45:| `EC-TIMEOUT` | a bounded stage was killed by its wall clock | timeout is not a subject verdict |

name: twenty-create-app
description: Use when scaffolding a Twenty app.
---

# When To Use

Pick this skill when the user wants to start a brand-new Twenty app from scratch. Representative triggers:

- "I want to build a Twenty app"
- "scaffold a new Twenty app"
- "start a new Twenty plugin / extension / integration"
- "create a CRM extension for Twenty"
- "set up a Twenty app project"
- "bootstrap a Twenty app called X"

Do not use this skill when the app already exists — use `develop-app` to add features, `manage-app` for sync/deploy/troubleshooting, `publish-app` for marketplace prep, or `use-twenty-mcp` to query workspace data.

# Quickstart an App

For background on how Twenty apps work — the SDK packages, remotes, sync lifecycle, and rendering model — read `../twenty-official-references/references/concepts/how-apps-work.md`.

Use this as the default way to start an app unless the user gives different instructions.

## Why A Twenty Instance Is Needed

Before scaffolding, explain to the user that a Twenty app is not a standalone application — it is a package that extends a running Twenty instance. During development, the app's entities (objects, views, front components, logic functions) are synced to a Twenty instance where they are registered, rendered, and executed. Without a connected instance, there is nothing to sync to, no workspace to test in, and no way to verify the app works.

## Choose A Twenty Instance

By default, ask the user for the URL of their existing Twenty instance (e.g. `https://app.twenty.com` or a self-hosted URL). Mention that if they don't have one yet, you can spin up a local instance with Docker instead.

The two options are:

1. **Existing Twenty instance (default)** — the user provides the URL of a running Twenty server (self-hosted or cloud, e.g. `https://app.twenty.com`). The scaffolder authenticates via OAuth on that instance. Best when the user already has a workspace with data they want to develop against.
2. **Local instance with Docker (fallback)** — only when the user has no Twenty instance available. The scaffolder starts a disposable local Twenty server on `http://localhost:2020` through Docker. Requires Docker Desktop to be installed and running.

If the user does not provide a URL, ask first whether they have a Twenty instance URL to use; only fall back to Docker if they explicitly say they don't have one.

Before scaffolding, repeat back the app's purpose in one sentence and its expected shape: standard objects extended, any custom objects, whether it needs UI, whether it needs workflows or post-install seeding. Scaffolding is one-way — confirming here avoids re-scaffolds later.

## Scaffolding

First, ask the user for the app name if they did not provide one.

The directory name must contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens. Transform the entered name to lowercase and replace spaces with hyphens when needed.

For an existing Twenty instance (default):

```bash
npx create-twenty-app@latest <app-name> --url <twenty-instance-url>
```

The `--url` flag authenticates via OAuth on the provided instance. The scaffolder opens a browser for the OAuth flow, then stores the credentials as a remote in `~/.twenty/config.json`.

Only if the user has no Twenty instance and wants to try locally with Docker:

```bash
npx create-twenty-app@latest <app-name>
```

This omits `--url` and starts a disposable local Twenty server through Docker.

The scaffolder handles everything: it creates the project, enables corepack, installs dependencies, initializes Git, authenticates with the target instance, runs an initial sync, and opens the generated app page when possible.

If the user provides a package name, display name, or description, pass them through:

```bash
npx create-twenty-app@latest <app-directory> --name "<package-name>" --display-name "<display-name>" --description "<description>"
```

Supported create-time options are `--name`, `--display-name`, `--description`, `--url`, and `--authentication-method`.

## After Scaffolding

When the scaffolder completes, the app is fully created, synced, and installed. The job is done.

Do not run any follow-up validation commands after scaffolding unless the user asks for them. Do not run `yarn twenty apply`, `yarn test`, `yarn lint`, or other validation just to prove the scaffold worked; the scaffolder already performed the initial sync. If the user asks to run tests later, switch to `develop-app` or `manage-app` guidance and run the full suite against the isolated test instance with `TWENTY_API_URL=http://localhost:2021`.

Report to the user that the app was created successfully and is ready for development. Then stop. Wait for the user to ask for the next action.

The scaffolder generates a placeholder page at `src/front-components/main-page.tsx` plus its page layout and navigation menu item. In `develop-app`, delete all three before the first deploy unless the app actually needs UI. Do not stack additional pages on top of the placeholder.

## Docker Fallback Troubleshooting

Use this only when the user opted into the Docker fallback and it fails because Docker is missing or not running.

The preferred recovery is to ask the user for an existing Twenty instance URL and rerun the scaffolder with `--url <twenty-instance-url>` — this skips Docker entirely.

If the user still wants the local Docker path and Docker is missing, share this download link: `https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/` and ask them to install Docker Desktop.

# Next Steps

Only proceed to these when the user explicitly asks:

- Use `develop-app` when the user wants to add objects, fields, logic functions, roles, views, navigation, page layouts, skills, agents, or front component registrations.
- Use `../twenty-official-references/references/design/front-component-ui.md` when the user wants to design or improve the UI of a Twenty front component.
- When the user later makes changes to app entities, use `yarn twenty apply` to sync those changes. See the `manage-app` skill for sync workflow.

<!-- TOC: Critical Rules | Quick Workflow | Essential Commands | bv Integration | References -->

# beads-br — Beads Rust Issue Tracker

> **Non-invasive:** br NEVER runs git commands. Sync and commit are YOUR responsibility.

## Critical Rules for Agents

| Rule | Why |
|------|-----|
| **ALWAYS use `--json`** | Structured output for parsing |
| **NEVER run bare `bv`** | Blocks session in TUI mode |
| **Export check before commit** | Mutations auto-flush JSONL by default; `br sync --flush-only` is the final check |
| **Git is YOUR job** | br only touches `.beads/` directory |
| **No cycles allowed** | `br dep cycles` must return empty |

## Quick Workflow

```bash
# 1. Find work
br ready --json

# 2. Claim it
br update bd-abc123 --status in_progress

# 3. Do work...

# 4. Complete
br close bd-abc123 --reason "Implemented X"

# 5. Final export check, then commit (git is always manual)
br sync --flush-only
git add .beads/ && git commit -m "feat: X (bd-abc123)"
```

## Essential Commands

```bash
# Lifecycle
br init                              # Initialize .beads/
br create "Title" -p 1 -t task       # Create (priority 0-4)
br update <id> --status in_progress  # Claim work
br close <id> --reason "Done"        # Complete
br reopen <id>                       # Reopen if needed

# Querying (always use --json for agents)
br ready --json                      # Actionable work (not blocked)
br list --json                       # All issues
br blocked --json                    # What's blocked
br search "keyword"                  # Full-text search
br show <id> --json                  # Issue details

# Dependencies
br dep add <child> <parent>          # child depends on parent
br dep cycles                        # MUST be empty!
br dep tree <id>                     # Visualize dependencies

# Sync (mutations auto-flush JSONL and reads auto-import by default; git is never automatic)
br sync --flush-only                 # DB → JSONL (final check before git commit)
br sync --import-only                # JSONL → DB (after git pull)

# System
br doctor                            # Health check
br config list                       # Show configuration
```

## Priority Scale

| Priority | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| 0 | Critical |
| 1 | High |
| 2 | Medium (default) |
| 3 | Low |
| 4 | Backlog |

## bv Integration

**CRITICAL:** Never run bare `bv` — it launches interactive TUI and blocks.

```bash
# Always use --robot-* flags:
bv --robot-next                      # Single top pick
bv --robot-triage                    # Full triage
bv --robot-plan                      # Parallel execution tracks
bv --robot-insights | jq '.Cycles'   # Check graph health
```

## Agent Mail Coordination

Use bead ID as thread_id for multi-agent coordination:

```python
file_reservation_paths(..., reason="bd-123")
send_message(..., thread_id="bd-123", subject="[bd-123] Starting...")
# Work...
br close bd-123 --reason "Completed"
release_file_reservations(...)
```

## Session Ending Pattern

```bash
git pull --rebase
br sync --flush-only
git add .beads/ && git commit -m "Update issues"
git push
git status  # Verify clean
```

## Anti-Patterns

- Running `br sync` without `--flush-only` or `--import-only`
- Forgetting sync before git commit
- Creating circular dependencies
- Running bare `bv`
- Assuming auto-commit behavior

## Storage

```
.beads/
├── beads.db        # SQLite (primary)
├── issues.jsonl    # Git-friendly export
└── config.yaml     # Optional config
```

## Troubleshooting

```bash
br doctor                    # Full diagnostics
br dep cycles                # Must be empty

# Complete Beads Prompt Reference

## Table of Contents
- [Plan to Beads Conversion](#plan-to-beads-conversion)
- [Polishing Prompts](#polishing-prompts)
- [Fresh Session Prompts](#fresh-session-prompts)

## Plan to Beads Conversion

### THE EXACT PROMPT — Full Version

```
OK so now read ALL of [YOUR_PLAN_FILE].md; please take ALL of that and elaborate on it and use it to create a comprehensive and granular set of beads for all this with tasks, subtasks, and dependency structure overlaid, with detailed comments so that the whole thing is totally self-contained and self-documenting (including relevant background, reasoning/justification, considerations, etc.-- anything we'd want our "future self" to know about the goals and intentions and thought process and how it serves the over-arching goals of the project.). The beads should be so detailed that we never need to consult back to the original markdown plan document. Remember to ONLY use the `br` tool to create and modify the beads and add the dependencies. Use ultrathink.
```

**Replace** `[YOUR_PLAN_FILE].md` with your actual plan filename.

### THE EXACT PROMPT — Short Version

```
OK so please take ALL of that and elaborate on it more and then create a comprehensive and granular set of beads for all this with tasks, subtasks, and dependency structure overlaid, with detailed comments so that the whole thing is totally self-contained and self-documenting (including relevant background, reasoning/justification, considerations, etc.-- anything we'd want our "future self" to know about the goals and intentions and thought process and how it serves the over-arching goals of the project.)  Use only the `br` tool to create and modify the beads and add the dependencies. Use ultrathink.
```

**Use when:** Plan is already in context from earlier conversation.

---

## Polishing Prompts

### THE EXACT PROMPT — Polish (Standard)

```
Reread AGENTS dot md so it's still fresh in your mind. Check over each bead super carefully-- are you sure it makes sense? Is it optimal? Could we change anything to make the system work better for users? If so, revise the beads. It's a lot easier and faster to operate in "plan space" before we start implementing these things!

DO NOT OVERSIMPLIFY THINGS! DO NOT LOSE ANY FEATURES OR FUNCTIONALITY!

Also, make sure that as part of these beads, we include comprehensive unit tests and e2e test scripts with great, detailed logging so we can be sure that everything is working perfectly after implementation. Remember to ONLY use the `br` tool to create and modify the beads and to add the dependencies to beads. Use ultrathink.
```

### THE EXACT PROMPT — Polish (Full with Plan Reference)

```
Reread AGENTS dot md so it's still fresh in your mind. Then read ALL of [YOUR_PLAN_FILE].md . Use ultrathink. Check over each bead super carefully-- are you sure it makes sense? Is it optimal? Could we change anything to make the system work better for users? If so, revise the beads. It's a lot easier and faster to operate in "plan space" before we start implementing these things! DO NOT OVERSIMPLIFY THINGS! DO NOT LOSE ANY FEATURES OR FUNCTIONALITY! Also make sure that as part of the beads we include comprehensive unit tests and e2e test scripts with great, detailed logging so we can be sure that everything is working perfectly after implementation. It's critical that EVERYTHING from the markdown plan be embedded into the beads so that we never need to refer back to the markdown plan and we don't lose any important context or ideas or insights into the new features planned and why we are making them.
```

**Use when:** You want to ensure nothing from the original plan was lost.

### Polishing Protocol

```
Round 1 → Significant changes expected
Round 2 → Moderate changes
Round 3 → Fewer changes
...
Round 6-9 → Steady-state (minimal changes)

If flatlines early → Start fresh CC session
Cross-model review → Have Codex/GPT 5.5 do final round
```

---

## Fresh Session Prompts

When polishing flatlines, start a brand new Claude Code session:

### THE EXACT PROMPT — Step 1: Re-establish Context

```
First read ALL of the AGENTS dot md file and README dot md file super carefully and understand ALL of both! Then use your code investigation agent mode to fully understand the code, and technical architecture and purpose of the project.  Use ultrathink.
```

### THE EXACT PROMPT — Step 2: Review Beads

```
We recently transformed a markdown plan file into a bunch of new beads. I want you to very carefully review and analyze these using `br` and `bv`.
```

### THE EXACT PROMPT — Step 3: Polish

Then follow with the standard polish prompt.

---

## Test Coverage

### THE EXACT PROMPT — Add Test Beads

```
Do we have full unit test coverage without using mocks/fake stuff? What about complete e2e integration test scripts with great, detailed logging? If not, then create a comprehensive and granular set of beads for all this with tasks, subtasks, and dependency structure overlaid with detailed comments.
```

**Use when:** Feature beads exist but test coverage is unclear.

| Model | Role | Prompt |

| Claude/Opus | Primary creation | Plan to Beads (Full) |
| Claude/Opus | Multiple polish rounds | Polish (Standard) |
| Codex/GPT 5.5 | Final review | Polish (Standard) |
| Gemini | Alternative perspective | Fresh Session → Review |

# mcp__mcp_agent_mail_send_message — mcp-agent-mail/send_message

Send a Markdown message to one or more recipients and persist canonical and mailbox copies to Git.

Discovery
---------
To discover available agent names for recipients, use: resource://agents/{project_key}
Agent names are NOT the same as program names or user names.

What this does
--------------
- Stores message (and recipients) in the database; updates sender's activity
- Writes a canonical `.md` under `messages/YYYY/MM/`
- Writes sender outbox and per-recipient inbox copies
- Optionally converts referenced images to WebP and embeds small images inline
- Supports explicit attachments via `attachment_paths` in addition to inline references

Parameters
----------
project_key : str
    Project identifier (same used with `ensure_project`/`register_agent`).
sender_name : str
    Must match an agent registered in the project.
to : list[str]
    Primary recipients (agent names). At least one of to/cc/bcc must be non-empty.
subject : str
    Short subject line that will be visible in inbox/outbox and search results.
body_md : str
    GitHub-Flavored Markdown body. Image references can be file paths or data URIs.
cc, bcc : Optional[list[str]]
    Additional recipients by name.
attachment_paths : Optional[list[str]]
    Extra file paths to include as attachments; will be converted to WebP and stored.
convert_images : Optional[bool]
    Overrides server default for image conversion/inlining. If None, server settings apply.
    Note: sender attachments_policy "inline"/"file" always forces conversion/inlining.
importance : str
    One of {"low","normal","high","urgent"} (free form tolerated; used by filters).
ack_required : bool
    If true, recipients should call `acknowledge_message` after reading.
thread_id : Optional[str]
    If provided, message will be associated with an existing thread.
broadcast : bool
    Reserved for schema compatibility only. `broadcast=true` is intentionally
    rejected to prevent agent spam; address agents explicitly instead.
topic : Optional[str]
    Optional case-insensitive tag (1-64 ASCII characters). It must begin with an
    alphanumeric character; remaining characters may also include `.`, `_`, or `-`.
    Replies inherit the original message's topic.
sender_token : Optional[str]
    Registration token returned by `register_agent`. If provided and valid,
    the response includes `verified_sender: true`. If provided but mismatched,
    the call is rejected. If omitted, the message sends but with `verified_sender: false`.

Returns
-------
dict
    {
      "deliveries": [ { "project": str, "payload": { ... message payload ... } } ],
      "count": int,
      "verified_sender": bool
    }

Edge cases
----------
- If no recipients are given, the call fails.
- Unknown recipient names in the same project are auto-registered as placeholder agents (program/model `unknown`, profile archived) while MESSAGING_AUTO_REGISTER_RECIPIENTS is on (default) and the registration proof gate is off; otherwise the send fails fast. Register recipients first when they need a real identity.
- Non-absolute attachment paths are resolved relative to the project archive root.
- `broadcast=true` is intentionally rejected.

Do / Don't
----------
Do:
- Keep subjects concise and specific (aim for ≤ 80 characters).
- Use `thread_id` (or `reply_message`) to keep related discussion in a single thread.
- Address only relevant recipients; use CC/BCC sparingly and intentionally.
- Prefer Markdown links; attach images only when they materially aid understanding. The server
  auto-converts images to WebP and may inline small images depending on policy.

Don't:
- Send large, repeated binaries—reuse prior attachments via `attachment_paths` when possible.
- Change topics mid-thread—start a new thread for a new subject.
- Broadcast to "all" agents unnecessarily—target just the agents who need to act.

Examples
--------
1) Simple message:
```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"5","method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"send_message","arguments":{
  "project_key":"/abs/path/backend","sender_name":"GreenCastle","to":["BlueLake"],
  "subject":"Plan for /api/users","body_md":"See below."
}}}
```

2) Inline image (auto-convert to WebP and inline if small):
```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"6a","method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"send_message","arguments":{
  "project_key":"/abs/path/backend","sender_name":"GreenCastle","to":["BlueLake"],
  "subject":"Diagram","body_md":"![diagram](docs/flow.png)","convert_images":true
}}}
```

3) Explicit attachments:
```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"6b","method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"send_message","arguments":{
  "project_key":"/abs/path/backend","sender_name":"GreenCastle","to":["BlueLake"],
  "subject":"Screenshots","body_md":"Please review.","attachment_paths":["shots/a.png","shots/b.png"]
}}}
```

Idempotency
-----------
idempotency_key : Optional[str]
    Optional client key that makes this send safe to retry after a timeout. A retry
    with the same key and identical arguments replays the original result (same
    message id) with "idempotent_replay": true and does NOT create a second message
    or a second git-archive write. Reusing the key with different arguments returns
    error type IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT. Keys are scoped per (project, tool) and
    retained for a configurable window (default 24h; AM_IDEMPOTENCY_RETENTION_SECS).
    Omit to preserve default behavior.

## Schema
```ts
type Args = {
  auto_contact_if_blocked?: boolean | null;
  sender_token?: string | null;
  sender_name: string;
  body_md: string;
  subject: string;
  cc?: string[] | null;
  attachment_paths?: string[] | null;
  ack_required?: boolean | null;
  thread_id?: string | null;
  importance?: string | null;
  bcc?: string[] | null;
  topic?: string | null;
  convert_images?: boolean | null;
  idempotency_key?: string | null;
  project_key: string;
  broadcast?: boolean | null;
  to: string[];
};
```
Execute by writing JSON to xd://mcp__mcp_agent_mail_send_message.

7:## Purpose
8:
9:This document defines the target first-contact journey for Clutter-Free Spaces:
10:form submissions, inbound texts/photos, calls, emails, referrals, Google
11:discovery, Instagram discovery, and future Google Business Profile messages all
12:normalize into one CRM pane.

14:The system should help Joshua and Chanel see every new request, respond through
15:the right channel, and move the lead through the same professional-organizer
16:process without losing track of consent, safety, budget, scheduling, proposal
17:readiness, or follow-up ownership.
18:
19:This is a process contract and validation checklist. It does not approve new
20:customer sends, SMS automation, 10DLC registration, Squarespace edits, form
21:edits, n8n workflow activation, proposal sends, invoice sends, or non-button
22:Hermes database writes.

60:## Current Public First Touches
61:
62:The live site currently exposes these first-contact paths:
63:
64:- Call/text: `406-285-1525`
65:- Hero CTA: `Text Us a Photo Now`
66:- Process copy: Step 1 is call or text, with no pressure and no commitment.
67:- Bottom CTA: call, text, or fill out the form.
68:- Public promise: the form receives a response within 24 hours.
69:- Contact/email/social discovery paths exist through the site footer.
70:
71:The existing public voice is the right posture: calm, practical, low-pressure,
72:no-judgment, and direct about the next step. The single-pane process should
73:preserve that instead of turning the first contact into a long interrogation.
74:
75:## North Star
76:
77:Every first contact becomes one actionable CRM lead card with:
78:
79:- Source attribution.
80:- Contact identity.
81:- Preferred contact channel.
82:- Allowed contact channels.
83:- SMS consent state, separate from email/call preference.
84:- Timeline of inbound/outbound events.
85:- Mattermost alert in the `leads` channel.
86:- Next best action.
87:- Missing-facts checklist.
88:- Safety status.
89:- Scheduling status.
90:- Proposal readiness status.
91:- Owner and SLA.
92:- Audit trail of every button press, draft, send, skip, or N/A decision.
93:
94:Hermes acts like an employee in this system. Hermes can read, summarize,
95:recommend, draft, and press approved buttons. Hermes should not bypass button
96:capabilities with direct arbitrary CRM writes, customer sends, provider changes,
97:or admin-only toggles.

99:## Channel Model
100:
101:### Website Form
102:
103:Target behavior:
104:
105:1. Prospect submits a website form.
106:2. Website shows a thank-you state.
107:3. Submission normalizes into the CRM.
108:4. The current production intake path sends an email acknowledgement from
109:   `contact@clutter-free-spaces.com` when the acknowledgement path is enabled.
110:5. Mattermost receives a sanitized lead alert.
111:6. Hermes can summarize the lead and suggest the next button.
112:7. Joshua or Chanel sends any substantive first response manually in V1.
113:
114:Do not add new SMS/email automation from a form submission until send gates,
115:template approval, opt-out handling, and consent receipts are live. The existing
116:intake acknowledgement email is a production behavior and must stay covered by
117:provider-health checks and owner-reviewed copy.
118:

120:
121:- `apps/cfs-form` currently requires a phone field and stores
122:  `preferred_contact` / `allowed_contact_methods`.
123:- I did not find an explicit SMS consent receipt field in the current form
124:  schema.
125:- Therefore, a submitted phone number should not be treated as consent for
126:  business-initiated SMS automation.
127:- The public forms domain and exact public form path were validated during the
128:  2026-07-10 Joshua Test3 run.
129:
130:### Inbound SMS Or Photo
131:
132:Target behavior:
133:
134:1. Prospect texts the CFS number.
135:2. Telnyx signs and posts the inbound event to the CFS webhook.
136:3. CRM finds an existing contact by phone or creates an unmatched inbound queue
137:   item for review.
138:4. Mattermost receives a sanitized `New text lead` alert when the sender is
139:   unknown or needs follow-up.
140:5. The CRM lead card shows the message summary and asks Joshua/Chanel to decide
141:   the next step.

143:Current behavior proven on 2026-07-10:
144:
145:- Telnyx webhook URL is configured.
146:- Telnyx signing key is configured via API.
147:- Vercel production has Telnyx API key, webhook public key, webhook URL, from
148:  number, and messaging profile id.
149:- Inbound SMS can land in `cfs_conversation_log` when the sender phone matches
150:  exactly one `cfs_contacts.primary_phone_e164`.
151:- Unknown inbound SMS does not currently create a CRM lead. It no-writes because
152:  the webhook resolver requires an existing unique contact match.

154:Required before SMS is truly single-pane:
155:
156:- Add an `unmatched_inbound_sms` review path or equivalent lead creation flow.
157:- Preserve sender privacy in Mattermost.
158:- Record whether the customer initiated the SMS conversation.
159:- Record opt-out state and STOP/HELP behavior.
160:- Keep any automatic SMS response disabled until 10DLC and consent gates pass.

162:### Phone Call
163:
164:Target behavior:
165:
166:1. Prospect calls CFS.
167:2. If answered, Chanel/Josh records a call note or converts the call to a lead.
168:3. If missed/voicemail, the system creates a callback task.
169:4. Mattermost gets a callback-needed alert if the call cannot be resolved
170:   immediately.
171:5. CRM records whether the first response was call done, voicemail left, or
172:   needs callback.
173:
174:V1 rule:
175:
176:- Do not automate outbound phone calls.
177:- If preferred contact is phone, create a Chanel/Josh call task.
178:- Hermes can draft a call script and mark the call outcome only through approved
179:  buttons.

181:### Email
182:
183:Target behavior:
184:
185:1. Email inquiry creates or updates a CRM lead.
186:2. Mattermost alert links to CRM.
187:3. Hermes drafts a calm first response.
188:4. Joshua/Chanel reviews and sends.
189:5. CRM records sent/skipped/manual edit outcome.

191:V1:
192:
193:- Email-only live-send testing may go to Joshua as test client.

195:
196:### Instagram, Google, Referrals, Existing Clients

198:Target behavior:
199:
200:- Manual or integrated source creates the same CRM lead card.
201:- Source attribution records Instagram, Google Business Profile, referral,
202:  repeat client, or unknown.

207:## Consent And SMS Compliance
208:
209:This is not legal advice. It is the operational compliance posture the product
210:should enforce until Joshua/Chanel get formal legal review if needed.
211:
212:### Consent States
213:
214:Use explicit states instead of treating a phone number as permission:
215:
216:- `unknown`: no SMS permission record.
217:- `customer_initiated_sms`: customer texted CFS first; reply is allowed only
218:  for the relevant conversation.
219:- `form_sms_opt_in`: customer checked a separate SMS opt-in box on a form.
220:- `verbal_sms_opt_in`: Chanel/Josh recorded verbal consent during a call or
221:  in-person conversation.
222:- `service_sms_allowed`: operational service texts allowed.
223:- `marketing_sms_allowed`: marketing/newsletter texts allowed. This must be
224:  separate from service messages.
225:- `sms_opted_out`: do not send SMS except legally required confirmation if
226:  applicable.
227:- `sms_not_allowed`: customer declined SMS or no valid consent exists.
228:
229:### Form Checkbox Requirement
230:
231:If the website form asks for SMS permission, it should use a separate,
232:unchecked-by-default checkbox. It must not be bundled with phone calls, email,
233:terms acceptance, privacy policy acceptance, or the ability to submit the form.

239:organizing inquiry, scheduling, and project updates at the number I provided.
240:Message frequency varies. Message and data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt
241:out or HELP for help. Consent is not a condition of purchase. Privacy Policy
242:and Terms apply.
243:```
244:
245:If marketing/newsletter SMS is ever added, it should be a separate checkbox and
246:likely a separate 10DLC campaign/use case.
247:
248:### 10DLC Before Scale
249:
250:Before CFS uses Telnyx for routine business-initiated SMS from the CRM:
251:
252:1. Register/verify the CFS brand.
253:2. Register the right 10DLC campaign use case.
254:3. Provide representative sample messages.
255:4. Provide opt-in documentation.
256:5. Provide opt-out and HELP language.
257:6. Provide message frequency estimates.
258:7. Provide Privacy Policy and Terms links.
259:8. Associate the CFS Telnyx number to the approved campaign.
260:9. Verify STOP/HELP behavior and suppression before live customer sends.
261:
262:Do not combine service texts, project updates, appointment reminders, review
263:requests, referral requests, and newsletters into one vague SMS campaign.

# Post-Compact Reminder

> **The problem:** When Claude Code compacts context, all detailed instructions vanish. The agent forgets project conventions, in-progress work, and coordination state. Without a hook, the first post-compact action is always wrong.

## Pre-Setup Checklist

- [ ] Claude Code installed with hooks support (v1.0+)
- [ ] `~/.claude/settings.json` exists and is valid JSON
- [ ] Decide which files the agent must re-read after compaction
- [ ] Identify project-specific context (AGENTS.md, brand rules, etc.)
- [ ] State directory exists: `mkdir -p ~/.local/state/claude-agents-reminder`

## How It Works

The system uses a 3-script marker pattern:

```
PreCompact hook           → writes marker file with timestamp
  ↓ (compaction happens)
SessionStart:compact      → injects immediate recovery prompt
  ↓ (first user message)
UserPromptSubmit hook     → checks marker, injects one-shot reminder, deletes marker
```

**Why three scripts?** SessionStart:compact fires during compaction itself (context already gone). UserPromptSubmit fires on the NEXT user message — catching cases where SessionStart's output gets lost in the compaction summary.

## Which Hook Pattern Do I Need?

| Situation | Pattern | Scripts |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| Single developer, one project | **Basic** | SessionStart:compact only |
| Multi-project with AGENTS.md | **Standard** | All 3 scripts (marker pattern) |
| Swarm agents with Agent Mail | **Full** | Standard + inbox check + bead status |
| Workers with file reservations | **Full + reservations** | Standard + reservation re-check |

---

## Standard Pattern (Recommended)

### 1. Create the marker script

```bash
cat > ~/.local/bin/claude-precompact-marker << 'SCRIPT'
#!/bin/bash
MARKER_DIR="$HOME/.local/state/claude-agents-reminder"
mkdir -p "$MARKER_DIR"
date -Iseconds > "$MARKER_DIR/compact-pending"
# Capture in-progress work for compaction context
bd list --status=in_progress --limit 10 2>/dev/null
SCRIPT
chmod +x ~/.local/bin/claude-precompact-marker
```

### 2. Create the recovery prompt

```bash
cat > ~/.local/bin/claude-post-compact-reminder << 'SCRIPT'
#!/bin/bash
cat << 'EOF'
<post-compact-reminder>
Context was just compacted. Please:
1. Re-read AGENTS.md in the current project (if exists)
2. Re-read ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md for global conventions
3. Re-read ./CLAUDE.md for project-specific rules
4. Check for in-progress work: `bd list --status=in_progress`
</post-compact-reminder>
EOF
SCRIPT
chmod +x ~/.local/bin/claude-post-compact-reminder
```

### 3. Create the one-shot checker

```bash
cat > ~/.local/bin/claude-check-compact-marker << 'SCRIPT'
#!/bin/bash
MARKER="$HOME/.local/state/claude-agents-reminder/compact-pending"
if [[ -f "$MARKER" ]]; then
    rm -f "$MARKER"
    cat << 'EOF'
<system-reminder>
Context was just compacted. Re-read AGENTS.md and check in-progress work.
</system-reminder>
EOF
fi
SCRIPT
chmod +x ~/.local/bin/claude-check-compact-marker
```

### 4. Wire into settings.json

Add to `~/.claude/settings.json` under `"hooks"`:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreCompact": [{
      "matcher": "",
      "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "$HOME/.local/bin/claude-precompact-marker"}]
    }],
    "SessionStart": [{
      "matcher": "compact",
      "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "$HOME/.local/bin/claude-post-compact-reminder"}]
    }],
    "UserPromptSubmit": [{
      "matcher": "",
      "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "$HOME/.local/bin/claude-check-compact-marker"}]
    }]
  }
}
```

**Deep dive:** [HOOK-PATTERNS.md](references/HOOK-PATTERNS.md) | **Customization:** [CUSTOMIZATION.md](references/CUSTOMIZATION.md)

---

## Customizing the Recovery Prompt

Tailor the recovery prompt to your project:

| Project Type | Add to recovery prompt |
|-------------|----------------------|
| Frontend (React/Next.js) | Re-read brand rules, check CSS variable conventions |
| Backend (API) | Re-read API conventions, check migration state |
| Swarm agent | Check Agent Mail inbox, verify file reservations |
| Infrastructure | Re-read deployment state, check running services |

## Verification Checklist

After setup, verify each component:

- [ ] `cat ~/.claude/settings.json | jq '.hooks.PreCompact'` — shows marker command
- [ ] `cat ~/.claude/settings.json | jq '.hooks.SessionStart'` — shows compact matcher
- [ ] `cat ~/.claude/settings.json | jq '.hooks.UserPromptSubmit'` — shows checker command
- [ ] `ls -la ~/.local/bin/claude-*compact*` — all 3 scripts exist and are executable
- [ ] `~/.local/bin/claude-precompact-marker && ls ~/.local/state/claude-agents-reminder/` — marker created
- [ ] `~/.local/bin/claude-check-compact-marker` — marker deleted, reminder emitted
- [ ] Run `/compact` in Claude Code — verify recovery prompt appears
- [ ] Send a message after compact — verify one-shot reminder fires

---

## Anti-Patterns

| Anti-Pattern | Fix |
|-------------|-----|
| Putting recovery logic in PreCompact | PreCompact runs BEFORE compaction — output is lost. Use SessionStart:compact. |
| Not deleting the marker file | One-shot pattern: delete marker FIRST, then emit. Prevents duplicate triggers. |
| Giant recovery prompts (>500 tokens) | Keep it short — long prompts waste the fresh context window. Point to files, don't paste content. |
| Skipping the marker pattern | SessionStart:compact alone misses cases where its output gets summarized. The marker + UserPromptSubmit is the safety net. |
| Hardcoding project paths | Use relative paths (./AGENTS.md) or env vars. Hooks must work across projects. |
| Not testing after setup | Run `/compact` manually to verify the hooks fire correctly. |
| Relying on memory after compaction | Agents remember NOTHING specific. The hook must tell them exactly what to re-read. |
| No bead/task status in recovery | Without `bd list --status=in_progress`, the agent picks up wrong work. |
| Same prompt for all projects | Use project-specific CLAUDE.md — the hook says "re-read CLAUDE.md" which differs per project. |

---
